channel.title: Said & Checked: Florida — AskAmerica
channel.description: What officeholders said each day from or about Florida, and which statements government data supports, contradicts or rules out.

item.title: Said & Checked, Florida, 2026-11-20: none false or contradicted, 2 unsettled (Carlos Gimenez, Ashley Moody)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Carlos Gimenez, U.S. Representative: “simple to make and detonate” Unsettled. NRC and CDC fact pages describe a dirty bomb as conventional explosives combined with radioactive material that would rarely release enough radiation to kill, but do not say how easy one is to make or detonate; a 2011 Congressional Research Service report calls such devices "much simpler to build" than nuclear weapons while listing obstacles to an effective attack. These pages were read through a summarizing fetch tool, not directly, and the DHS fact sheet could not be read.
  • Ashley Moody, U.S. Senator: “after 40 days in the NICU, he passed away from being denied a heart transplant.” Unsettled. Search summaries of family and news accounts describe Zion Sarmiento of Ocala spending 40 days in a NICU and being refused by three Florida transplant centers before dying in October 2021 at about 16 weeks old, so the 40 days and the refusals fit but the sequence in the sentence is not confirmed; no account was read directly.

7 statements by 3 officeholders. 6 checked: 4 supported, 2 unsettled · 1 not checkable.

item.title: Said & Checked, Florida, 2026-11-15: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (Ron DeSantis)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Ron DeSantis, Governor of Florida: “What they are doing is not mandated by Florida law” Unsettled. This turns on how the statute is read. Florida's SB 1134, effective Jan. 1, 2027, bars a municipality from funding or promoting activities designed with reference to ethnicity, among other categories, and exempts content-neutral event permits and recognition of state and federal holidays. It names no parades and requires no cancellation.
